Dataset: 1345 drugs from dataset3, each one name-matched to ChEMBL and then standardised with RDKit — largest fragment, neutralised, metals refused.

Training data: one ChEMBL set per biological target. 189 targets carry enough measured chemistry to be fitted at all (20 compounds minimum); 98 were refused for too little, with the reason recorded rather than a model fitted anyway. 236,374 cleaned compound/activity pairs in total, one standard_type per target (never Ki and IC50 mixed), binding assays only, exact relations only, duplicates merged by median, replicates spanning more than one log unit dropped.
A fingerprint bank of 236,374 training compounds (Morgan r=2, 2048 bits) is what a new molecule is compared against. It is built once and is the only thing the router reads.
Predictors: 16 declared whole-molecule descriptors, fixed before any model was fitted — mw, clogp, clogp_sq, mr, tpsa, hbd, hba, rotb and 8 more.
Measured human PK from dataset3 (fu, Vdss, clearance, MRT, half-life) travels with every row under a measured_ prefix and is never fitted against. It is a measurement, not a descriptor.

Output: one CSV. One column per predictor, therapeutic index last. 649 rows carry an index; the remaining 696 are in the file with an empty index and a stated reason, the largest being “no validated series model and the fallback is below q2=0.25” (167).
Workflow: Endpoint (OECD 1): p_activity(primary target) - p_toxicity(hERG, CHEMBL240), both -log10 mol/L. Higher is a wider margin over the cardiac liability. This is not LD50/ED50, not a clinical therapeutic index, not dose-aware, not safety evidence.

One global model assembled out of many local ones. There is no single pooled equation and no single ranking: a molecule is scored by the local model fitted on its own target, and the ranking happens inside that target. Ranking an antipsychotic against an antibiotic would be arithmetic without meaning, so the CSV never does it.

Routing, step one: ChEMBL's mechanism-of-action table, where it records one and that target has a fitted model. Step two, for everything else: structure alone. The query is compared against every eligible model's training set and routed on the Morgan r=2 top-5 mean Tanimoto against each local model's training set. The chemist never has to name the target.

The router is allowed three answers, and two of them are not an answer: route it, call it ambiguous when several neighbourhoods are within the margin, or abstain when nothing clears the scope floor. On this batch: routed by ChEMBL's recorded mechanism 581, routed on structure 212, called ambiguous 23, abstained 372, no structure to route 157. A routed target is an inference from chemical similarity and the row says so; it is never recorded as a measurement.

Routing thresholds are calibrated on the training sets only, leave-one-out, with no drug labels: scope floor 0.4536, margin 0.01. The same calibration is candid about the hard part — for 28% of training compounds the single most similar neighbourhood is not their own target, so structural similarity alone cannot be treated as a target assignment. The router is tested separately from the models it routes to, against a baseline that always answers with the largest model, because an easy conditional is not evidence of valid routing.

Inside each local model, three tiers in order. 1. Measurement, where ChEMBL has one. 2. A Hansch equation for the congeneric series the molecule belongs to. 3. A declared non-linear fallback on the same descriptors, labelled non-mechanistic. A molecule reaches a series equation only by belonging to that series: median Morgan Tanimoto at or above that series' own membership floor, the 10th percentile of its internal pairwise similarity.

Acceptance (OECD 4): series — n ≥ 15, median similarity ≥ 0.55, r² ≥ 0.6, q²(leave-one-out) ≥ 0.5, shuffled q² < 0.05. Terms capped at n/5 and chosen on AICc, so the criterion selected on is never the criterion reported. Result: 190 of 2238 candidate series passed; 139 of 189 targets produced a usable fallback, q² 0.25–0.72 with whole chemical families held out.

Applicability domain (OECD 3): descriptor range for a series equation, kNN distance at the 95th percentile for the fallback. 371 ranked rows sit inside it; the rest say so in their own row. Every index is also re-derived from its own two columns before the file is written, and the run stops rather than ship a row whose arithmetic does not hold.
Software: RDKit: standardisation (LargestFragmentChooser, Uncharger), Crippen logP and molar refractivity, TPSA, QED, Gasteiger partial charges, Bemis–Murcko scaffolds, Morgan fingerprints at radius 2, and BRICS fragmentation for the matched-pair cores the router can route on.
scikit-learn: the declared non-linear fallback (random forest, 300 trees) and the standardiser behind the kNN applicability domain. Nothing else.

Ordinary least squares, leave-one-out q², AICc, the y-randomisation test and the Tanimoto search are written out in ti/fit.py and ti/router.py rather than imported, so every figure in the report can be traced to the line that computed it.
Data sources: ChEMBL web API (activities, mechanisms, structures) and dataset3 for the batch and its measured human PK. No PubChem structures.

Reproducibility: ti/resolve.py → ti/pull_training.py → ti/fit.py --all → ti/registry.py → ti/cores.py → ti/router_test.py --calibrate → ti/router_test.py --benchmark → ti/rank.py → ti/report.py → ti/publish.py. Every stage caches, the random seed is fixed, and audit.json carries the input hashes and library versions that produced the CSV.
